intelligence.human_view: Three failures in one message, and they are one correction. First: the work was never finished and never shared — "he never finished. He never shared with me. I've never seen any update." Done that he has not seen is not done; an update that never reached his eyes never happened. "I don't know where you're at" is the verdict on a lane that worked without showing. Second: the document meant to show him the work could not be gotten through — "so many double pages." Duplicates are not thoroughness; they are a document he cannot read, and a document he cannot read is no update at all. Third: what he did see is flat — icons "how flat they are how bright they are they don't look real. Look how undynamic that looks." Flat, bright, unreal, still. The fix is named in his own words: "we need to make that all dynamic." Dynamic is not decoration here — it is the Real Object Law and the living-intelligence standard applied to the calendar inner pages: real objects with depth, light with volume, press and movement, alive on the page. The calendar inner pages are also the first landing named by SN-3207's scorecard question — what can we learn from the Smart Mail page to take over to creating the calendar inner pages. The answer starts here: finish it, share it, one clean document, all dynamic.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you build a beautiful calendar for your dad, but you never finish it, and you never show it to him — and the paper you did show him had every page printed twice, so he couldn't get through it. And the little pictures on it are flat and too bright, like stickers, not like real things. He says: finish it, show it to me, give me one clean paper without doubles — and make the pictures real and moving, like things you can touch. That's the whole job.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, he never saw the calendar pages at all — the work was never finished and never shared with him, and the document had so many pages printed twice over that he couldn't get through it. "If you have done it I haven't seen it," he said — and he's right, dear, work he hasn't seen isn't done. And the icons on it are flat and too bright, they don't look real at all, nothing moves. So we finish it properly, we share it so he sees it, we give him one clean document with no doubles — and we make it all dynamic, dear, real and alive, like proper objects you could touch, not flat pictures.
intelligence.naya_view: NEVER FINISHED, NEVER SHARED, NEVER SEEN. A DOCUMENT WITH DOUBLE PAGES IS NO UPDATE AT ALL. FLAT, TOO BRIGHT, UNREAL, UNDYNAMIC — MAKE IT ALL DYNAMIC. FINISH IT. SHARE IT. ONE CLEAN DOCUMENT. REAL OBJECTS, ALIVE.
